critique: Every candy and every letter runs the same copy-pasted keyframe recipe (identical drop/squash/jostle curves, just offset by 0.1s or 0.12s), so the piece feels mechanical, not elastic. The 'jostle' is a tiny horizontal nudge with no contact between shapes. The letters launch up from y=860 through the candy cluster, which causes about 2.3s of messy overlaps (p and ! cross the violet star and pink square at 3.18s). The letters also squash around their centre, not their baseline, so they never read as landing on a trampoline.

Vary each element's drop height, timing and spring values, and anchor squash to the bottom edge. Have the letters drop from above onto a clear baseline below the candy, with a real compress-and-launch bounce, and make the shapes visibly bump into their neighbours. Replace the 0.3s dead hold and the stiff whole-group rotation (4.2s to 5s) with staggered per-element idle wiggles: small offset rotation and scale loops on each letter and candy.
